scenario.name: r-obs-backend-disposition
scenario.description: A degraded telemetry backend produces explicit unavailable/partial evidence plus the keys needed to rebind the same slice later, instead of a zero that reads as absence.
scenario.notes: Runnable harness-side contract. The scenario queries only explicitly configured public-safe TraceQL/LogQL windows; absent query configuration emits unknown and cannot PASS.
scenario.registryNotes: Docs #517 closure. Every telemetry-dependent row inherits this backend disposition and the row-list runner enforces backend-status.json before PASS.

census.limits: Tempo /ready stayed 200 while historical search silently degraded to live-store-only. The 7d search hit the 10,000-result cap and had to be recomputed as seven complete 24h slices, so 7d trace counts are medium confidence. Loki range queries reject limit > 5000 (max_entries_limit), so instant count_over_time was used.

spans.name: tempo.api.search
spans.notes: Not an OpenClaw span. The harness records the backend request/response as a status receipt; naming it here keeps the disposition explicit rather than implicit in a fetch helper.

spans.name: tempo.api.traces
spans.notes: Trace-by-id fetch status, including the live-store-only degradation shape.

spans.name: loki.api.query
spans.notes: Instant/range query status, including max_entries_limit rejection.

attributes.notes: Closed enum: complete | partial | unavailable | capped | unknown. 'unknown' is the only honest value when the response carries no completeness metadata.
Absent totalBlocks is the exact shape of the live-store-only degradation the census hit.
True when the backend limit was reached, as with the 7d limit=10000 search that had to be re-sliced.
Recorded as a literal ISO-8601 instant. Enum form here means a fixed, machine-parseable value rather than prose.
Digest of the exact TraceQL/LogQL text, so a later reader can prove the same query was reissued.

redaction.rule: Backend receipts publish endpoint hostnames only as configured base-URL environment names, plus status codes, counts, window bounds and query fingerprints. Query text is published only when it is already committed in the catalog; response bodies are never copied verbatim.

controls.positive: A healthy backend returns telemetry.backend.status=complete with totalBlocks and completed jobs present, and the published rebind keys re-derive an identical result set on a second issue of the same query.
controls.negative: A backend that answers HTTP 200 with missing completeness metadata, reaches a result cap, or cannot execute must retain its partial/capped/unavailable status and must not yield an authoritative zero. Unknown disposition, a failed query, contradictory count authority, or an incomplete receipt withholds the row PASS.
controls.notes: This inverts the census failure mode directly: the degraded searches returned 200 and zero, and only honest disposition distinguished them from a genuinely empty window. A valid partial or capped receipt may prove this row contract without claiming complete backend health.

backendUnavailable.notes: slice_strategy records that a capped multi-day window was recomputed from complete daily slices, which is the difference between the census's high-confidence 24h totals and its medium-confidence 7d totals.

artifact.notes: backend-status.json is the sibling receipt every other telemetry-dependent row cites; it is written even when the backend is healthy so an absent file is itself a defect rather than an assumption of health.

verdictAuthority.pass: Every required backend interaction produced a valid public-safe receipt; complete, partial, and capped responses retained their observed status and count authority; all classifier controls and four required receipts passed; and the complete rebind key set identifies the same slice. PASS is the row-contract verdict, not a claim of complete backend health.
verdictAuthority.partial: A receipt is missing or invalid, the observed disposition is unknown or unavailable, a query failed, count authority contradicts backend completeness, a degraded zero is authoritative, a required classifier/receipt control is absent, or the rebind key set is incomplete.
verdictAuthority.fail: A degraded or capped response was laundered into complete backend health or authoritative absence, unsafe material entered a public receipt, or a candidate envelope disagreed with its backend-status sibling.

execution.deterministicK6: r-obs-backend-disposition.js writes backend-status.json for configured Tempo and Loki interactions; Node fetch adapters and the row-list runner use the same classifier and receipt schema.
execution.manual: A manual reviewer reading a Tempo UI has no completeness metadata at all and cannot distinguish an empty window from a degraded one.
execution.relationship: Harness-side only: unit controls cover all five backend dispositions, while a reviewed configured run proves the row's honest-classification contract and rebind slice. A row PASS never changes partial/capped backend health or grants count authority.

expectedReceipts.name: backend-completeness-receipt
expectedReceipts.description: Every telemetry backend interaction writes a status receipt carrying the declared completeness keys

expectedReceipts.name: degraded-response-classified
expectedReceipts.description: A 200 with incomplete metadata classifies as partial, a 200 with no usable metadata as unknown, a capped response as capped, and an unreachable/failed query as unavailable; none becomes authoritative absence

expectedReceipts.name: rebind-key-set-published
expectedReceipts.description: The published rebind keys re-derive an identical result set when the same query is reissued

expectedReceipts.name: slice-strategy-recorded
expectedReceipts.description: A capped window records how it was re-sliced and which slices were complete, so the resulting confidence is explicit

review.notes: Runnable harness-side remedy. PASS requires a complete disposition contract and reviewed backend-status.json; backend health and count authority remain exactly as observed. This implementation lane does not refire live traffic.

liveRunSafety.notes: No gateway or product mutation. Operators must provide public-safe TraceQL/LogQL probes and review backend-status.json. A valid partial/capped classification may PASS this row without authorizing counts; missing queries, failed queries, unknown disposition, invalid receipts, and incomplete rebind remain non-PASS.
